News stories wrongly treated Gall-Peters as the only equal-area projection, despite a consensus that it is inappropriate for small-scale mapping.
Equal Earth is an equal-area pseudocylindrical projection developed by Patterson, Jenny and Šavrič in 2018.
In Equal Earth, parallels are straight and the poles are 0.59247 times the length of the equator.
Equal Earth was quickly adopted by the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies.
In March 2017 Boston Public Schools adopted the Gall-Peters projection; the controversy over its polar distortion led Šavrič, Jenny and Patterson to create Equal Earth.

The UN General Assembly adopted resolution A/80/L.104 'Correct the Map' on 4 September 2026 by 164 to 1 with 6 abstentions.
The resolution does not ban Mercator or impose a replacement; it encourages equal-area maps when relative size matters.
The US, the only country to vote against, said the resolution promoted an 'ideological agenda' and was a distraction from genuine problems.
